sections.h2: Which office in Wooster files a Wayne County deed?
sections.html:
Look for the Recorder behind the Administration Building's first-floor doors, 428 West Liberty Street, Wooster, OH 44691, or phone 330-287-5460. The county site describes the post as keeper of legal documents, chiefly real estate papers: deeds, mortgages, liens. Subdivision plats are also filed there.

The Auditor, Treasurer, Board of Revision and Map Office occupy the same building. Wooster serves a county of roughly 555 square miles. Lawmakers drew the county in 1808, and it began operating in 1812. The Census Bureau lists 116,758 residents for July 2025.

sections.h2: Which stops come before the Recorder in Wayne County?
sections.html:
A short route is posted on the Auditor's real estate page, and a deed that skips a stop tends to come back unrecorded.

  • Draft the deed, then present it at the Map Office.
  • Carry it to the Auditor, where the conveyance and transfer charges are paid.
  • Last, file at the Recorder's counter.

The state's value statement sits behind the Auditor's stop. R.C. 319.202 requires a declaration of value from the grantee before endorsement. An exempt transfer states its reason in place of a value, using the exemption form DTE 100(EX) from the Auditor's library.

sections.h2: What is the Wayne County conveyance charge at the Auditor?
sections.html:
The Auditor's page prints $4.00 per thousand dollars of price and $0.50 per parcel, applied after the price is bumped up to the next $100. The Auditor's Tools menu includes a Conveyance Fee Calculator for the arithmetic.

Unpaid taxes can stall a closing. Phone the Treasurer at 330-287-5450 for a payoff, and see the delinquent list online. The Auditor, 330-287-5430, answers conveyance questions from 8:00 am on weekdays.

sections.h2: What does the Wayne County Recorder charge to record?
sections.html:
The table reproduces the Auditor's list, which follows R.C. 317.32, in which each of the base and housing trust fund shares is $17 for pages one and two and $4 for every page after. A county may also layer on a preservation surcharge capped at $5; ask the Recorder if the total below has one.

Recording charges as the Wayne County Auditor prints them
ItemCharge
First two pages$34.00
Each additional page$8.00
Marginal notation$4.00
Copies$2.00
Standardization guideline fee$20.00

That $20.00 line is aimed at papers that break the layout rules of R.C. 317.114, so check margins and ink with the Recorder before you sign.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau say about Wayne County households?
sections.html:
QuickFacts reports 44,365 households sharing 47,538 housing units, with 2.53 people in each household, and owners hold 76.6 percent of the homes.

  • Middle owner-held home value: $222,100.
  • Middle rent: $881 a month.
  • Middle household income: $73,574.
  • Share who stayed at the same address for a year: 90.2 percent.
  • Building permits during 2025: 232.

The Auditor's home page counts roughly 59,000 parcels, so most recorded deeds touch only a small slice of them in any year.

sections.h2: What should arrive at the Recorder's counter with a Wayne County deed?
sections.html:
Take the endorsed original, parcel numbers and a check. Because the Treasurer's FAQ says some name changes require a new deed, compare the owner's name on the Auditor's parcel record with the deed.

  • Land records at the Recorder are indexed by document type and parties.
  • A mortgage release is its own recording, with a marginal reference charge under the statute.
  • The Auditor's parcel search and GIS parcel viewer show earlier owners, acreage and last sale before the deed is written.

sections.h2: What does the value statement cover on a Wayne County sale?
sections.html:
The statute counts the full price paid or owed, mortgage and vendor's lien amounts included. A gift is valued at its likely open market price. Willfully misstating value is prohibited.

Two more questions ride along. One covers owner-occupied credit and homestead reductions. The other covers agricultural use valuation and any recoupment charge. A yes to either means both parties confirm the amount has been accounted for.

sections.h2: How does a tax due date interact with a Wayne County closing?
sections.html:
Installment bills are issued in January or February and again in June or July. The Treasurer's last days for 2026 were February 26 and July 30; a 10 percent penalty follows, and half is returned if the balance clears within 10 days.

If a deed records in the same week a bill comes due, put in writing who pays. Bank payments faced earlier cutoffs (February 2 and July 13 in 2026). Partial payments are accepted and all go toward the upcoming bill.

sections.h2: Which four Wayne County phone lines does a seller need?
sections.html:
• Recorder, 330-287-5460.
  • Auditor, 330-287-5430.
  • Treasurer, 330-287-5450.
  • Board of Revision, 330-287-5433.

Call ahead with your parcel number in hand. The first handles recording, the second conveyance and parcel records, the third balances and payments, and the fourth valuation complaints. All answer from the same Wooster address.

sections.h2: Does a Wayne County sale let the new owner file a fresh value complaint?
sections.html:
Usually, yes. R.C. 5715.19 generally bars a second complaint on one parcel inside an interim period. Exceptions follow an arm's length sale, a casualty loss, a substantial improvement or a 15 percent occupancy change after the earlier lien date. A sale can therefore reopen the door for a parcel the seller already contested.

Filing opens each January 1, and for tax year 2026 the Auditor lists January 1 to March 31, 2027. Signatures must be notarized, which Auditor staff can usually do in person. The second half bill is held until the Board rules, and the first half stays payable on time.

sections.h2: What do Wayne County taxes look like after the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Assessed value is 35 percent of market value, multiplied by the district rate and trimmed by a reduction factor. The owner-occupied credit has its own application, form DTE 105C, in the Auditor's library.

Rates differ by district, and the Treasurer's website charts them all.

sections.h2: Which online tools can a Wayne County seller use before recording?
sections.html:
• Auditor: a parcel search and map, a conveyance calculator, a tax estimator, a levy estimator, sales reports and a delinquency report, plus downloadable forms.
  • Treasurer: payment through Autoagent online or at 1-844-615-1900, and monthly or semi-annual ACH direct debit for parcels that owe current taxes.
  • Recorder: the county's page lists the office address and phone, so a call to 330-287-5460 settles questions about what a particular paper needs.

Run the sales report and tax estimator first. They show what nearby parcels sold for and what the levies on your district would produce, which helps when you write the value into the statement.

sections.h2: How has Wayne County grown, according to the Census Bureau?
sections.html: The county counted 114,520 people in 2010 and 116,894 in 2020, and its July 2025 estimate of 116,758 sits slightly below the 2020 base. Land area is 554.79 square miles and density was 210.7 people per square mile in 2020, up from 206.4 in 2010. Median age was 39.0 at the 2020 count, with 24.0 percent of residents under 18 and 18.6 percent 65 or older.

faqs.q: Where in Wooster do I file a Wayne County deed?
faqs.a: With the Recorder, 330-287-5460, in the Administration Building. Get the Auditor's endorsement first.

faqs.q: What recording fees does the Auditor's page list for Wayne County?
faqs.a: The printed list is $34.00 for two pages, $8.00 per added page, $4.00 per marginal notation, $2.00 per copy and a $20.00 standardization fee. A preservation surcharge of up to $5 is optional under state law.

faqs.q: What does the Auditor take at the Wayne County conveyance step?
faqs.a: The Auditor prints $4.00 per $1,000 of price and $0.50 per parcel. The grantor owes the conveyance charge.

faqs.q: Is the Auditor's stop before or after the Recorder in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Before. The sequence is Map Office, Auditor, then Recorder.

faqs.q: Who gives a tax payoff on a Wayne County parcel?
faqs.a: The Treasurer, at 330-287-5450. Its website also shows a delinquent list.
